chapter: Police work, brass bands and carnival
title: Son Wilson's playing style and tonk music
summary: Allen asks whom Son Wilson sounded like; Williams says he was a real tonk blues man like Clayton, Chris Kelly and Howard, unlike today's refined imitators.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Well we're getting all off of music. But what about Son Wilson? Did he play like anybody? Oh yeah. He played a job, a lot of parties. No, did he sound like anybody? Was he on Chris
Kelly's auto? Yeah, he was a real blues man, you know, a real tunk.
Something like Chris. Like Clayton. Like Clayton.

Yeah, Clayton. Clayton and Chris was real tunk man, you know what I mean? Howard too, he played a lot of tunk music too. You know? They got some of them guys trying to play, trying to imitate you know. They don't have the tone, the execution.
